articleTitle: Implications of broadband satellite BoD algorithms on TCP performance
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: Most next generation satellite systems propose to use a bandwidth on demand (BoD) mechanism to efficiently share a limited radio spectrum among a large number of users. The design of a BoD system needs to consider a range of engineering issues: the anticipated number of users, interactions with other subsystems, and contradictory the design goals of optimising system utilisation and latency offered. The efficiency of a satellite system supporting an TCP/IP service is highly dependent on the delay and the variation of the delay experienced by the TCP transport protocol. This paper therefore investigates transport layer pathologies in BoD satellite networks.

articleTitle: Quality of service for personal satellite multimedia
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: As the terrestrial mobile networks are moving towards third generation (3G) systems with the capability of delivering IP (Internet protocol) based multimedia services. Any satellite system that is designed to offer complementary coverage terrestrial 3G systems is expected to offer similar services and Quality of Service (QoS). A satellite system faces a number unique issues as compared to a terrestrial system. The solutions found for terrestrial systems may not necessary be applicable to a satellite system. This paper addresses the issues and challenges of designing a satellite system offering a good QoS.

articleTitle: A bandwidth efficient modem for personal satellite terminals
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: Personal satellite communications is constrained by both bandwidth and power, with mobility requirements demanding compact, low cost and highly efficient user terminal equipment, whilst system capacity requirements demand an efficient usage of the limited satellite bandwidth available. This paper describes a bandwidth efficient modulation (BEM) scheme that combines power and bandwidth efficiency for multi-user communication over a satellite channel. Results of initial performance tests generated using a modem simulator are presented, illustrating the effect of frequency and timing errors on the working of the scheme.

articleTitle: Time-series of attenuation on EHF and SHF fixed satellite links derived from meteorological and forecast data
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: A method for deriving time-series of attenuation on fixed satellite or terrestrial links is described. The method uses meteorological forecast data and radar data and hence permits time coincident derivations for multiple sites that include the spatial correlation properties inherent in weather systems. The success of the technique depends upon insertion of the short interval temporal properties (varying typically over 1 second to 15 minutes) that are statistically independent between stations. The technique has immediate application to simulation of the performance of multimedia satellite to earth links and has longer-term significance in terms of operational real-time performance prediction.

articleTitle: Personal broadband satellite systems and services
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: The Internet boom of the latter half of the last decade fuelled a proliferation of projects for satellite-based broadband Internet delivery systems. Some of these projects were based on existing satellite infrastructure, primarily offered by already established DBS operators; many more of these projects were new ventures seeking to finance sophisticated, bespoke satellite systems with the seemingly endless supply of venture capital that was available for investment in any new project associated with the Internet. The continued growth of the Internet is seen to provide a basis for investment in wideband Internet delivery and it is quite clear that terrestrial delivery systems such as cable and DSL will only be able to partially meet the demand for personal, broadband Internet access.

articleTitle: Personal broadband satellite for the small office/home office user
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: In the Scottish Highlands, access to telecommunication services is limited in terms of supplier, affordability and availability. This part of the UK, with it's low population density and rugged terrain, is truly a challenge when it comes to communications infrastructure, despite various governmental initiatives to assist. An announcement by BT to launch a broadband satellite service to the Highlands & Islands and Northern Ireland is, therefore, an interesting development. Will the system work and will it appeal to the small office/home office user? Will it mean less investment in other technologies? This paper is presented from both an end-user and a market perspective. From the end user view, we look at how these systems actually work for a SOHO operator - considering what it's like to use in everyday circumstances, and would a user pay for this service over and above ISDN? From a practical viewpoint, how easy is it to set up, what is the equipment like and what are the restrictions? Also, how does the user address the planning regulations and what are the consequences for installation times?.

articleTitle: Effective medium access control for satellite broadband data traffic
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: This paper explores some of the techniques and issues associated with the design of an effective medium access control (MAC) protocol for a geostationary satellite channel. Two satellite MAC schemes are described, combined free/demand assignment multiple access (CFDAMA) and burst targeted demand assignment multiple access (BTDAMA) and their performance is evaluated for both Poisson and self-similar data traffic. Simulation results show that the effectiveness of different MAC techniques is heavily dependent on the nature of the traffic to be supported. It is shown that the CFDAMA scheme can provide good delay/utilisation performance of a satellite channel for Poisson traffic but poorer performance for the highly bursty self-similar traffic. The BTDAMA scheme on the other hand provides good delay/utilisation performance for self-similar traffic but is less suited to handling Poisson traffic.

articleTitle: Use of performance enhancing proxies in mesh topologies
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: A number of techniques have been described in the literature for improving TCP performance over satellite links. Generally these are designed to mitigate the effect of the link latency on TCP performance. This paper considers the deployment of performance enhancing proxies in more generalised mesh and partial mesh topologies which include satellite links. Results are presented and interpreted for asymmetric connection-splitting proxies.

articleTitle: BTopenworld satellite broadband from concept to launch
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Personal Broadband Satellite (Ref. No. 2002/059)
abstract: BTopenworld is one of the first mass market UK Internet service providers (ISP) to grasp the challenge which is currently facing the satellite communication industry, namely the migration from providing traditional trunk connections and broadcasting into the emerging field of delivering local access Internet services. This paper reviews the commercial drivers from both the ISP and end customer perspective surrounding the delivery of broadband Internet and multimedia services via satellite, including positioning of such services in relation to existing and future broadband terrestrial offerings. An explanation of the various technological solutions that presently exist to deliver such services is then given, for example the relative merits of hybrid and two way satellite solutions and the use of performance enhancing proxies to enhance the end user Internet browsing experience. This paper specifically draws on the real life experiences gained from taking the BTopenworld broadband satellite service from concept to launch and also covers, for example, VSAT licensing and local planning aspects.
